'''Korek Telecom''' ({{langx|ckb|کۆڕەک تیلیکۆم}}) is an [[Iraq|Iraqi]] [[telecommunications company]] in [[Erbil]], [[Kurdistan Region]].<ref name="veconomist" >{{cite news|title=A new war in Iraq, now between Shia Arabs and Kurds|url=https://www.economist.com/news/middle-east-and-africa/21730328-iraqi-leaders-act-retake-city-and-its-oilfields-kurds-new-war|newspaper=[[The Economist]]|date=16 October 2017}}</ref> In August 2026, all of its assets were ordered to be seized by the Iraqi [[Communications and Media Commission (Iraq)|Communications and Media Commission]] (CMC). Due to outstanding debts and unresolved legal issues, CMC began procedures to dissolve the company on 1 November 2026.

==History==
In March 2011, France Télécom (now [[Orange S.A.]]) acquired a 20% indirect stake in Korek Telecom.<ref>{{cite web|last=Goldstein |first=Phil |url=http://www.fiercewireless.com/europe/story/france-telecom-invests-175m-iraqi-operator-korek/2011-03-16 |title=France Telecom invests €175m in Iraqi operator Korek |publisher=FierceWireless |date=2011-03-16 |accessdate=2013-08-06}}</ref>

On Jan 1, 2015, Korek launched<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.korektel.com/services/data-offers/extra-g |title=Extra G |publisher=Korek Telecom}}</ref> 3G in Iraq after winning one of the three [[3G]] licenses awarded by the [[government of Iraq]]. On Dec 16, 2015, Korek became the first operator in Iraq to launch [[Free Basics]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.korektele.com/services/data-offers/freebasics-com | title=Free Basics | publisher=Korek Telecom | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104092020/http://www.korektele.com/services/data-offers/freebasics-com | archive-date=2016-01-04 }}</ref> in Iraq in partnership with [[Internet.org]] and [[Facebook]].

In March 2023, the company was implicated in a major corruption scandal and found guilty of bribing regulators, self-dealing, diversions of corporate assets, sham loans, and other illegal schemes.<ref> {{ cite web|url=https://www.whitecase.com/news/press-release/white-case-secures-us165-billion-arbitration-award-iraq-telecom-limited|title=White & Case secures US$1.65 billion arbitration award for Iraq Telecom Limited|publisher=White&Case}}</ref> The Paris-based [[International Court of Arbitration]] found Korek and its founder and controlling shareholder [[Sirwan Barzani]] guilty of ‘fraud and corruption’ and awarded $1.65 billion in damages to Iraq Telecom Limited, a joint venture of Kuwaiti company Agility and French Orange Group, and International Holdings.<ref> {{ cite web|url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/14750-icc-finds-korek-liable-to-pay-damages-to-iraq-telecom.html|title=ICC finds Korek liable to pay damages to Iraq Telecom|publisher=Developing Telecoms}}</ref>

==Shutdown==
Due to the company's failure to pay debts (worth over US$1 billion) owed to the government, in November 2023 [[Communications and Media Commission (Iraq)|Iraq's telecommunications regulator]] (CMC) blocked all incoming and outgoing communications between Korek and other carriers as a punitive measure. In September 2024, Korek announced that it had reached an agreement with CMC over its financial obligations, however, the block ordered by CMC on external communications remained. In 2025, a judicial committee was appointed to issue recommendations regarding the legal battle between the regulator and the company which were approved by Iraqi authorities. This resulted in a financial settlement agreement being reached in June 2025 between the two parties.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://erbilweekly.com/korek-subscribers-fear-disruption-as-iraq-moves-to-shut-down-network/|title= Korek Subscribers Fear Disruption as Iraq Moves to Shut Down Network|website=Erbil Weekly|date= 12 August 2026}}</ref> 

However, in February 2026, CMC annulled the agreement reached in June and ordered Korek's internet services to be blocked, again due to the company's inability to comply with its financial obligations.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://thenewregion.com/posts/5540|title= Korek Telecom CEO slams Iraq's contract decision as 'unlawful,' vows legal action|website=The New Region}}</ref> Korek subsequently sued CMC over its decision to annul the settlement agreement at Baghdad's Rusafa Court of First Instance.

On 9 August 2026, following the expiration of Korek's operating contract, CMC ordered the full seizure of all movable and immovable assets belonging to Korek.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/931491/korek-accuses-iraqs-telecom-regulator-of-unlawful-campaign-as-shutdown-looms|title=Korek Accuses Iraq's Telecom Regulator of 'Unlawful' Campaign as Shutdown Looms|website=Kurdistan 24 |date=10 August 2026 }}</ref> Korek released a statement complaining about the actions taken against it and pleading to the Iraqi prime minister for intervention, citing the formal agreement reached in June 2025. According to CMC, Korek had violated the conditions of the agreement by failing to meet the legal and financial obligations therein, effectively rendering the agreement void.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rudaw.net/english/categories/kurdistan/1078752|title=Korek Telecom asks Iraqi PM to intervene over dispute with Iraqi telecom regulator|website=Rudaw |date=10 August 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://shafaq.com/en/society/Korek-Telecom-faces-complete-operational-shutdown|title=Korek Telecom faces complete operational shutdown|website=Shafaq News}}</ref> The procedures for the shutdown of the company began on 10 August 2026. On the same day, [[Masoud Barzani]] announced that he would visit the capital to discuss "a crucial matter". The visit was abruptly cancelled the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://ultrairaq.ultrasawt.com/%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AA%D9%83%D8%B4%D9%81-%D8%A3%D8%B3%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D8%AA%D8%A3%D8%AC%D9%8A%D9%84-%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B2%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8A-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A8%D8%BA%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A3%D8%AA%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1-%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%85%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%85/%D9%81%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1|title= مصادر تكشف أسباب تأجيل زيارة مسعود بارزاني إلى بغداد: "سيأتي مسرور لأمر حاسم"|website=Ultra Iraq|language=ar}}</ref> On 19 August 2026, CMC urged all Korek users to register with other licensed telecommunications operators and set up alternative authentication and recovery methods in order to avoid losing access to their accounts registered with Korek telephone numbers as well as avoid data loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rudaw.net/english/categories/iraq/1078904|title=Iraq telecom regulator urges Korek users to secure backup numbers for account access, recovery|website=Rudaw |date=19 August 2026 }}</ref> 

During the Baghdad International Dialogue Conference which was attended by Baleegh Abu Kalal, CMC's director of operations, he stated that 'digital sovereignty' belongs exclusively to the federal government, and that telecommunications companies in [[Kurdistan Region]] will pay the price for the debts they owe the government.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://ina.iq/ar/local/271514-.html|title= أبو كلل: السيادة الرقمية بيد السلطة الاتحادية ولا يمكن توزيعها|website=Iraqi News Agency|language=ar}}</ref> 

On 23 August 2026, Baghdad's Rusafa District Court issued a decision to temporarily suspend CMC's actions against Korek until a formal verdict is reached in court. The decision came after the regulator closed Korek's Baghdad headquarters and outlets in the city.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.964media.com/51508/|title=Court suspends regulator's action against Korek days after offices closed|website=+964 Media |date=23 August 2026 }}</ref> On 26 August 2026, the Rusafa District Court issued a ruling "overturning the injunction filed by the managing director of Korek Telecom and upholding the CMC’s decision to suspend operations with the company". The court found that Korek's petition lacked "procedural and legal grounds".<ref>{{cite web|url= https://thenewregion.com/posts/6341|title= Iraqi court upholds CMC's decision against Korek, says regulator|website=The New Region}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://rudaw.net/english/categories/iraq/1078999|title= Baghdad court clears way for suspension of Korek operations|website=Rudaw|date= 26 August 2026}}</ref>

On 3 September 2026, CMC closed Korek's offices and service centres in [[Najaf Governorate|Najaf]], [[Karbala Governorate|Karbala]], [[Qadisiyyah Governorate|Diwaniyah]] and [[Babylon Governorate|Babylon]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://en.964media.com/52025/|title= Korek closures extended to three more governorates|website=+964 Media|date= 3 September 2026}}</ref> On 6 September, the closures were extended to [[Kirkuk Governorate|Kirkuk]], [[Saladin Governorate|Saladin]] and [[Nineveh Governorate|Nineveh]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://en.964media.com/52156/|title= Korek office closures reaches eight governorates across federal Iraq|website=+964 Media|date= 6 September 2026}}</ref> On 13 September, CMC announced that Korek users had until 30 September to secure their accounts before their communications are shut down, stating: "once the specified deadline has passed, [CMC] will proceed to shut down Korek Telecom's [[telephone exchange]] in the capital Baghdad and the rest of Iraq's governorates in turn, as part of the regulatory and legal measures taken against the company".<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.pukmedia.com/AR/Details/190633|title= هيئة الإعلام والاتصالات تمهل مستخدمي كورك حتى نهاية أيلول|website=PUKmedia|language=ar}}</ref> On 18 September, Kurdistan Regional Government minister of communications stated that Korek will not cease operations in Kurdistan Region, since, according to the minister, no company can be shut down without consulting with the regional government.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://rudaw.net/english/categories/kurdistan/1079351|title= KRG minister says Korek Telecom to continue operating in Kurdistan despite Baghdad threats|website=Rudaw|date= 18 September 2026|quote=No party can shut down a Kurdistan-based enterprise without consulting with the KRG. We operate under a federal system—not a centralized or dictatorial system.}}</ref> On 28 September, Baghdad's Rusafa Court of First Instance ruled that the financial settlement agreement reached in June 2025 between the two parties remained valid, overturning CMC's decision to unilaterally annul it. In a statement released by CMC, it indicated that it would continue its closure of the company and that the ruling did not impede that, rather, that it merely obligated Korek to pay its debts while having no ruling regarding the legality of CMC's efforts to shut down the company.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://thenewregion.com/posts/6655|title= Iraqi court overturns regulator's nullification of financial settlement agreement with Korek|website=The New Region|quote=The ruling did not grant the company a license or renew its existing license. The settlement agreement remains in effect, meaning the company is still obligated to pay the established debts owed to the state, in addition to any other outstanding dues. The ruling does not exempt the company  from any of these obligations.}}</ref> On 30 September, CMC offered Korek an opportunity to resume operations if it pays an initial payment of debt worth 500 billion Iraqi dinars (US$382 million) as a sign of good faith.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://shafaq.com/en/society/CMC-sets-382M-payment-for-Korek-return|title= CMC sets $382M payment for Korek return|website=Shafaq News}}</ref>

On 6 October, CMC announced that the deadline for Korek's shutdown would be delayed by one month, to 1 November 2026, due to a request by the Iraqi parliament's communications committee. This was reportedly done in order to give Korek customers more time to secure their accounts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rudaw.net/english/categories/iraq/1079613|title=Iraqi regulator gives Korek one-month reprieve before shutdown: Statement|website=Rudaw}}</ref>

On 1 November 2026, formal procedures to shut down Korek began. CMC announced the closing of the company's switching centers in several governorates, resulting in cessation of service in 14 governorates. There were procedures underway to close all remaining ones.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thenewregion.com/posts/6987|title=Korek says may seek compensation over CMC measures|website=The New Region}}</ref>
